formCues: Load into a quarter squat before jumping
Rotate hips and shoulders together in the air
Land softly facing the opposite direction
Absorb landing with bent knees
setup: Stand tall with feet shoulder-width apart in open space with clearance on all sides.
commonMistakes: Rotating only the upper body, not the hips
Landing stiff-legged
Losing balance on the turn

formCues: Descend into a full-depth snatch-grip overhead squat
Press the bar overhead from the bottom position
Keep torso upright and core braced
Drive elbows forward under the bar
setup: Take a wide snatch grip on the bar in the front or back rack, squat down to full depth.
commonMistakes: Losing thoracic extension and rounding forward
Insufficient ankle/hip mobility causing heel lift
Pressing before reaching full squat depth

formCues: Feet shoulder-width apart, toes slightly out
Push hips back and bend knees together
Keep chest up and heels planted
Drive through mid-foot to stand
setup: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, arms extended forward or at sides for balance.
commonMistakes: Knees caving inward
Heels lifting off the floor
Not reaching full depth

formCues: Clean the dumbbell to shoulder in one motion
Brace core and press directly overhead
Keep hips square, avoid excessive lean
Lock out arm fully at the top
setup: Stand with a thick-handled dumbbell racked at one shoulder, feet planted shoulder-width.
commonMistakes: Using excessive lateral lean instead of controlled press
Not bracing the core before pressing
Uneven hip position causing loss of balance

formCues: Pull explosively to release hands from the bar
Clap quickly at the top of the pull
Re-grip the bar before descending
Control the lowering phase
setup: Hang from a pull-up bar with an overhand grip, arms fully extended.
commonMistakes: Insufficient pulling power leading to a failed re-grip
Swinging with momentum instead of explosive pull
Dropping uncontrolled after the clap

formCues: Keep knees bent and weight centered over skis
Shift weight to carve turns
Keep hands forward and visible
Absorb terrain changes with the legs
setup: Stand in ski boots and skis at the top of a slope with poles in hand, knees slightly bent.
commonMistakes: Leaning back on the heels
Locking the knees straight
Failing to look ahead down the slope

formCues: Explosively extend hips and knees to clean the dumbbell
Catch the dumbbell at the shoulder in a quarter squat
Dip and drive to jerk it overhead
Lock out arm and stabilize
setup: Stand over a dumbbell with feet hip-width apart, gripping the handle with one hand.
commonMistakes: Pulling with the arm instead of the legs and hips
Not dipping before the jerk drive
Catching the jerk with a soft, unlocked elbow

formCues: Let the weight roll down into the fingertips
Curl fingers to close the hand around the bar
Keep wrist neutral throughout
Move slowly and control the descent
setup: Sit holding a barbell or dumbbell with forearms resting on thighs or a bench, palms up.
commonMistakes: Using wrist flexion instead of finger flexion
Moving too fast and losing grip control
Using too much weight for the small muscles involved

formCues: Spread fingers against band or light resistance
Open hand fully then control the return
Keep wrist stable and neutral
Move slowly through full range
setup: Place a rubber band around fingertips or hold a light dumbbell in a rice bucket, hand relaxed.
commonMistakes: Using excessive resistance that limits range
Letting wrist move instead of isolating fingers
Rushing the extension phase

formCues: Drop into a deep squat with hands near feet
Explode upward and forward off both feet
Swing arms to assist the jump
Land softly back into a squat
setup: Stand with feet wide, squat down low with hands resting near the floor between the knees.
commonMistakes: Landing with straight knees
Not achieving enough hip depth before jumping
Jumping only vertically instead of forward

formCues: Widen knees out to the sides on all fours
Flex ankles with feet in line with knees
Lower hips back and down slowly
Breathe deeply and relax into the stretch
setup: Start on hands and knees, then gradually widen the knees apart while keeping shins parallel.
commonMistakes: Widening knees too fast, straining the groin
Letting feet turn outward instead of staying flexed
Holding tension in the shoulders instead of relaxing

formCues: Widen knees to a comfortable range
Keep hips sinking back and down
Support upper body on forearms
Hold and breathe without bouncing
setup: Kneel on the floor, widen the knees out to the sides with lower legs flat on the ground.
commonMistakes: Bouncing in the stretch instead of holding static
Overextending the range and straining adductors
Rounding the lower back excessively

formCues: Start bar at mid-thigh with flat back
Extend hips and knees explosively
Pull bar high and rotate elbows around fast
Catch on extended legs with no dip
setup: Stand holding a barbell at mid-thigh with a shoulder-width grip, knees slightly bent, back flat.
commonMistakes: Bending the elbows too early in the pull
Catching in a squat instead of muscling it up
Rounding the lower back during the hang position

formCues: Lift toes and forefoot off the ground
Walk forward balancing on heels only
Keep shins engaged and steps short
Maintain upright posture throughout
setup: Stand tall with feet flat, then raise the toes and balls of the feet off the floor.
commonMistakes: Letting toes drop back to the floor between steps
Taking overly long strides that break balance
Hunching forward instead of standing tall

formCues: Press kettlebell overhead while lying supine
Roll onto the side keeping arm vertical
Anchor the same-side leg across the body
Keep shoulder packed and stable
setup: Lie on your back holding a kettlebell pressed straight up over one shoulder.
commonMistakes: Letting the arm drift out of vertical alignment
Rolling too fast and losing shoulder stability
Failing to anchor the hips, causing the body to follow the roll

formCues: Place each foot on the opposite thigh crease
Lengthen the spine upward
Rest hands on knees, relax shoulders
Breathe slowly and stay still
setup: Sit on the floor with legs extended, then fold each leg to rest the foot on the opposite thigh.
commonMistakes: Forcing the fold without adequate hip mobility
Slouching the spine instead of sitting tall
Placing strain directly on the knee joint

formCues: Stack shoulder, hip, and hand in one vertical line
Press firmly through the fingertips for balance
Engage core and glutes to stay rigid
Shift weight subtly to correct balance
setup: Kick up into a freestanding handstand, then shift weight fully onto one hand while lifting the other.
commonMistakes: Overarching the lower back instead of staying hollow
Panicking and bailing instead of micro-adjusting balance
Insufficient shoulder and wrist strength causing collapse

formCues: Position shoulders under the pads, feet on platform
Lower under control along the arc path
Keep knees tracking over toes
Drive through the heels to extend
setup: Load the machine, step in with shoulders under the pads and feet set on the angled platform.
commonMistakes: Letting knees cave inward during the descent
Using too much weight and cutting range short
Bouncing out of the bottom position

formCues: Drive through the lead foot explosively
Extend hip fully and leave the box airborne
Land softly back on the same lead leg
Reset balance before repeating
setup: Stand facing a box or bench with one foot planted firmly on top.
commonMistakes: Pushing off the trailing leg instead of the lead leg
Landing with a stiff, locked knee
Using a box too high for controlled landing

formCues: Stand tall with a slight forward lean
Push and pull through the handles with the arms
Drive smoothly through the legs in an elliptical path
Maintain steady, controlled cadence
setup: Step onto the adaptive motion trainer, grip the moving handles, and begin a smooth striding motion.
commonMistakes: Gripping the handles too hard instead of guiding them
Slouching forward at the hips
Using jerky, uneven strides

formCues: Keep hips close to the wall
Push through the legs, not just pull with arms
Use straight arms to hang and conserve energy
Look ahead and plan the next hold
setup: Approach the boulder wall, chalk hands, and identify the starting hand and foot holds.
commonMistakes: Overgripping holds and fatiguing forearms early
Relying on arm strength instead of leg drive
Letting hips sag away from the wall

formCues: Keep knees bent and weight centered on the board
Shift weight between heel and toe edges to turn
Keep shoulders aligned with the board direction
Absorb bumps with ankle and knee flexion
setup: Strap both feet into the board bindings and stand sideways at the top of a slope.
commonMistakes: Leaning back and catching the heel edge
Locking the knees straight instead of staying flexed
Twisting shoulders out of alignment with the board

formCues: Start in a plank with shins on the ball
Roll the ball forward by lifting hips up
Keep arms straight and core braced
Return under control to plank
setup: Assume a plank position with hands on the floor and shins resting on top of a stability ball.
commonMistakes: Rounding the lower back instead of hinging at the hips
Letting the ball roll uncontrolled on the return
Bending the elbows during the pike

formCues: Kneel with forearms or hands on the ball
Brace core and roll the ball forward slowly
Keep hips extended, avoid sagging
Pull back to start using the abs
setup: Kneel on the floor with forearms resting on top of a stability ball in front of you.
commonMistakes: Letting the lower back arch and hips sag
Rolling out too far and losing control
Using shoulders to pull back instead of the core

formCues: Perform a standard push-up with control
Rotate into a side plank at the top
Reach the top arm straight toward the ceiling
Return to plank before the next rep
setup: Start in a push-up plank position with hands slightly wider than shoulders.
commonMistakes: Rotating the hips before completing the push-up
Sagging at the hips during the plank rotation
Rushing the rotation and losing balance

formCues: Rise up onto the balls of the feet
Take small controlled steps forward
Keep ankles stacked under the hips
Maintain tall, upright posture
setup: Stand tall with feet hip-width apart, then rise up onto the toes.
commonMistakes: Letting heels drop between steps
Taking strides too long to maintain balance
Rounding the shoulders forward

formCues: Lower into a wide-grip push-up position
Shift the body laterally toward one hand
Keep chest low and core tight throughout
Slide back across to the other side
setup: Start in a push-up plank with hands set wider than shoulder-width apart.
commonMistakes: Raising the hips during the lateral shift
Losing depth by not lowering fully
Moving too fast and losing shoulder control

formCues: Grip handles with palms facing each other
Brace core and press straight overhead
Keep torso upright, avoid excess lean
Lower under control to the chest
setup: Stand at the Viking press machine or landmine attachment, gripping the neutral handles at chest height.
commonMistakes: Leaning back excessively to press the weight up
Flaring elbows out too wide
Using leg drive instead of shoulder strength

formCues: Press lower back, head, and arms against the wall
Slide arms upward keeping contact with the wall
Avoid letting elbows or wrists lift off
Lower slowly back to start
setup: Stand with back flat against a wall, arms bent to 90 degrees pressed against the surface.
commonMistakes: Arching the lower back off the wall
Losing wall contact with the arms during the slide
Shrugging the shoulders up toward the ears

formCues: Step feet wide apart, toes forward
Hinge at the hips and fold forward
Let head hang relaxed toward the floor
Keep legs engaged and slightly soft at the knees
setup: Stand with feet wide apart, hands on hips, then hinge forward from the hips.
commonMistakes: Rounding through the lower back instead of hinging at hips
Locking the knees completely straight
Forcing the fold deeper than flexibility allows
